chicken-leg-drumstick-and-thigh-baked-or.title: Chicken leg, drumstick and thigh, baked or broiled, skin eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken legs, drumsticks and thighs (the portion of the thigh below the knee joint) are commonly prepared by baking or broiling. The skin is edible and adds flavor and a crisp texture. The product is rich in protein, B‑vitamins, iron and zinc.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken legs and thighs contain more fat than breast meat, making them juicier when cooked.
The skin is a source of collagen, which turns into gelatin during cooking.
In many cuisines (e.g., United States, China, Russia) chicken legs are often marinated before baking.
When cooked properly the skin becomes crispy while the meat stays tender.
Chicken thighs are favored for slow‑cooked dishes because they retain moisture.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Chicken legs and thighs provide complete protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: They contain vitamin B6 and niacin, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Iron, zinc and phosphorus are present, contributing to blood health and bone strength.

items.title: Collagen in the skin
items.content: The skin’s collagen can become gelatinous when cooked, potentially benefiting joint and skin health.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: The fat content makes the product a good source of calories for those with higher energy needs.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Excessive intake may contribute to weight gain and elevated cholesterol levels.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Chicken must be cooked thoroughly to eliminate Salmonella and Campylobacter.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: Sodium in marinades
items.content: Marinated cuts can be high in salt, which is a concern for hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Legs and thighs can be baked, grilled, braised or roasted. They are often marinated in a mixture of spices, oil and acid (lemon juice, vinegar) before cooking. The skin may be left on for a crispy crust or removed after cooking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Fresh meat should be kept in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for up to 2 days. Frozen portions store at –18 °C for up to 9 months. Thaw frozen chicken in the fridge, not at room temperature.

chicken-or-turkey-with-cream-sauce.title: Chicken or Turkey with Cream Sauce

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken or turkey with cream sauce is tender poultry meat sautéed and simmered in a rich sauce made from cream, butter, and seasonings. The dish offers a smooth, buttery flavor and aromatic herbs, suitable for everyday meals or special occasions.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The cream sauce is often deglazed with white wine or broth to deepen the flavor.
Traditionally served over pasta, rice, or mashed potatoes.
Turkey is leaner than chicken, but both provide high-quality protein.
Cream gives the sauce a velvety texture and helps retain moisture in the meat.
Some regional variations add mushrooms or a touch of mustard for extra complexity.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Chicken and turkey supply high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Poultry is abundant in niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, supporting metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Calcium from cream
items.content: The creamy sauce adds calcium, important for bone health.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: The dish fits low‑carb diets when paired with non‑starchy sides.

items.title: Beneficial fats
items.content: Cream contains monounsaturated fats that can be heart‑friendly in moderation.

items.title: Dairy allergy or lactose intolerance
items.content: The cream sauce may trigger reactions in people sensitive to milk proteins or lactose.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Cream and butter increase the dish’s calorie density; portion control is advised.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Using prepared broths or soy sauces can raise the sodium content.

items.title: Proper cooking
items.content: Poultry must be cooked thoroughly to eliminate the risk of salmonella.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Sauté chicken or turkey pieces until golden, then add onion, garlic, and herbs. Pour in cream (or a cream‑broth mix), bring to a simmer, and cook on low heat 15–20 minutes until the meat is tender. Optional additions include mushrooms, fresh parsley, or a sprinkle of grated Parmesan.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer keeping, freeze the cooled dish in a freezer‑safe bag for up to 2 months.

content.title: About
content.content: Cheez‑It crackers are small square-shaped snack crackers with a pronounced cheese flavor, made from wheat flour, vegetable oil and cheese. They are known for their crunchy texture and a light, slightly salty aroma. The product is popular as a quick snack and is often found in school lunch boxes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cheez‑It first appeared in the United States in 1921 under the Sunshine Biscuits brand.
The distinctive "plus‑plus" square‑hole shape was designed for easy biting.
The original recipe uses cheddar cheese, but today there are versions with other cheeses and spices.
The Cheez‑It brand has been owned by Kellogg Company since 2001.
In the 2020s the company released limited‑edition flavors such as "chipotle" and "spicy jalapeño".

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: The cheese component provides a modest amount of calcium, beneficial for bone health.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 present in the cheese is important for the nervous system and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Quick energy source
items.content: Crackers deliver fast‑acting energy from carbohydrates, convenient during active days.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: The amount of salt may be undesirable for individuals with hypertension.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: The product contains dairy cheese, which can trigger reactions in people allergic to milk.

items.title: Calorie dense
items.content: Because of carbs and fats, portion sizes should be moderated to avoid excess calorie intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cheez‑It crackers are convenient to eat straight from the bag, add to soups, salads, or snack platters. They can be crushed and sprinkled over casseroles or used in recipes to add a crunchy texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place with the package tightly sealed. For longer storage keep in an airtight container to prevent moisture absorption, which makes the crackers soft.

content.title: About
content.content: Canned lasagna with meat is a ready‑to‑eat dish packed in a sealed tin. It contains layers of pasta, tomato sauce, cheese, and ground beef or pork. Designed for quick heating in a microwave or on the stove while preserving flavor and texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Lasagna originated in Italy during the Middle Ages, and the canned version appeared in the United States in the early 20th century.
Canning allows the dish to be stored for 2‑3 years without added preservatives.
Grated Parmesan often creates a golden crust when the dish is heated.
Cans are usually made of aluminum with a food‑safe inner coating.
Meat lasagna is one of the most calorie‑dense ready meals, providing about 300‑350 kcal per serving.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Ground meat supplies a complete set of essential amino acids needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Red meat is rich in heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Hard cheese adds calcium, important for bone and tooth health.

items.title: Tomatoes – lycopene source
items.content: The tomato sauce provides lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that helps protect cells.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: High carbohydrate and fat content makes the dish a quick source of energy.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Canned foods often contain a lot of salt, which may be problematic for people with hypertension.

items.title: Calorie rich
items.content: The dish is calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable, especially on weight‑management diets.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese and other dairy ingredients can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Bisphenol A in packaging
items.content: Some aluminum cans may have trace amounts of BPA; choose products from reputable manufacturers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Open the can, pour the contents into a bowl and heat in the microwave for 3‑4 minutes or on the stove, stirring until evenly hot. For extra flavor, sprinkle additional cheese and bake for 5‑7 minutes until a golden crust forms.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep unopened cans in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, transfer leftovers to an airtight container and consume within 2‑3 days, storing them in the refrigerator.

pasta-with-tomato-based-sauce-and-added-.title: Pasta with Tomato-Based Sauce and Added Vegetables, Ready-to-Heat

content.title: About
content.content: Pasta with tomato-based sauce and added vegetables is a ready‑to‑heat meal containing durum wheat pasta, a sauce made from ripe tomatoes, carrots, zucchini, sweet pepper and green peas. The product is pre‑cooked, so it only needs to be heated in a microwave or on the stove.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The tomato sauce is prepared from ripe tomatoes, which are rich in lycopene – a powerful antioxidant.
Vegetables are added after a short blanching to preserve their bright colour and some vitamins.
The pasta is usually made from durum wheat, giving it a firm texture and lower glycemic impact.
The dish can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 5 days or frozen for up to 3 months.
Heat to at least 75 °C to ensure complete microbial safety.

items.title: Rich in lycopene
items.content: Tomatoes in the sauce provide lycopene, which supports heart health and may reduce the risk of certain cancers.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Durum wheat pasta supplies vitamin B1 (thiamine) and vitamin B3 (niacin), important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Fiber from vegetables
items.content: Carrots, zucchini and peas increase dietary fiber, promoting healthy digestion.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The meal contains potassium, magnesium and iron, essential for electrolyte balance and blood formation.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Prepared without added butter, the dish has minimal saturated fat content.

items.title: Gluten content
items.content: Durum wheat pasta contains gluten, making the product unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: The tomato sauce may contain added salt; those monitoring sodium intake should account for it.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes or other vegetables in the mix.

items.title: Improper heating
items.content: Insufficient heating can leave the product vulnerable to microbial growth.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the meal in the microwave for about 2–3 minutes, stirring halfway, or warm it on the stove until steam rises. Serve immediately; optional toppings include grated Parmesan or fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 0–4 °C in the original packaging for up to 5 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight container for up to 3 months. If frozen, ensure the product is fully thawed before reheating.

content.title: About
content.content: Ramen bowl is a ready‑to‑cook ramen kit in a bowl, containing dried noodles, a broth packet, aromatic seasonings and often dried vegetables. It is designed for quick preparation of hot ramen in 3–5 minutes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The NFS (National Food Service) brand distributes ramen bowls in over 20 countries.
Each serving provides about 350 kcal, making it a convenient snack for students and office workers.
The kit often includes a “black garlic” spice, popular in Asian cuisine.
Packaging is made from recyclable plastic, and some variants use biodegradable materials.
In Japan ramen bowls are frequently served with a boiled egg, but the NFS version omits the egg for longer shelf life.

items.title: Quick energy source
items.content: The dried noodles supply carbohydrates that are rapidly converted into energy, useful for an active lifestyle.

items.title: Protein content
items.content: A typical kit contains 8–10 g of protein, helping to maintain muscle mass.

items.title: Minerals and vitamins
items.content: The broth packet is fortified with iron, potassium and B‑vitamins that support metabolism.

items.title: Low fat
items.content: Most NFS ramen varieties contain less than 5 g of fat, suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Convenient storage
items.content: The dry product can be stored up to 12 months at room temperature without refrigeration.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: The broth packet may contain up to 900 mg of sodium, exceeding daily recommendations for people with hypertension.

items.title: Monosodium glutamate (MSG)
items.content: MSG is commonly added and can cause headaches or a tingling sensation in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: The kit may contain soy sauce, wheat and seafood; those with corresponding allergies should check the label.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large amounts of dry noodles can cause bloating in people with sensitive stomachs.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bring 400 ml of water to a boil, add the dried noodles and cook for 3–4 minutes. Drain some water if you prefer a thicker broth, then stir in the broth packet, seasonings and dried vegetables. Mix well and let stand for 1–2 minutes. Optionally top with a boiled egg, sliced green onion or chili.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the package in a dry, cool place away from direct sunlight. After opening, reseal tightly to prevent moisture ingress.

content.title: About
content.content: Scotch is a single‑malt or blended whisky produced in Scotland under strict regulations. It must be aged for at least three years in oak barrels, which gives it a distinctive aroma and flavor with notes of peat, smoke, fruit, and spice.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Scotch can be single malt or blended, depending on the number of distillates used.
Peat used to dry the barley imparts a characteristic smoky aroma, especially in island malts.
The oldest recorded Scotch, "Glenlivet 1862," has been aged for over 150 years.
Scotland is home to more than 130 distilleries, each with its own unique flavor profile.
Scotch is often used in cooking, adding depth to sauces, marinades, and desserts.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Polysaccharides and phenolic compounds in Scotch may help neutralize free radicals.

items.title: Moderate consumption supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Studies suggest small amounts of alcohol can raise HDL (good) cholesterol levels.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Traditionally enjoyed as a digestif, Scotch can stimulate gastric secretions.

items.title: Reduces stress
items.content: Moderate alcohol intake promotes relaxation and lowers cortisol levels.

items.title: Supports cognitive function
items.content: Some research links moderate drinking with slower cognitive decline in older adults.

items.title: Alcohol dependence
items.content: Excessive consumption can lead to addiction and serious health problems.

items.title: Blood pressure increase
items.content: Alcohol may temporarily raise blood pressure, especially in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Scotch can amplify the effects of sedatives and anticoagulants.

items.title: Caloric content
items.content: Alcohol provides 7 kcal/g, so large servings can contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Not recommended during pregnancy
items.content: Alcohol consumption during pregnancy raises the risk of fetal defects.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Scotch is typically served in small glasses (30–50 ml) at room temperature. It can be enjoyed neat, on the rocks, or in cocktails such as an Old Fashioned or a Rob Roy. For tasting, let the whisky breathe in the glass for a few minutes to release its aromas.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the bottle upright in a cool, dark place away from direct sunlight and temperature fluctuations. After opening, keep the cap tightly sealed to minimize oxidation.

content.title: About
content.content: Toddler formula, Nido Kinder is a milk-based infant formula designed for children from 1 year of age. It provides a balanced blend of proteins, fats, carbohydrates, vitamins, and minerals essential for growth and development.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The formula is fortified with iron and vitamin D to support bone development.
It contains prebiotics that promote a healthy gut microbiome.
Nido Kinder is produced according to international quality standards and undergoes strict safety testing.
Available in 400 g, 800 g and 1 kg packages.
The powder dissolves easily in warm water, creating a smooth, nutritious drink.

items.title: Supports bone growth
items.content: Rich in calcium and vitamin D, the formula helps build strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Balanced energy source
items.content: Complex carbohydrates and plant oils provide sustained energy.

items.title: Immune system support
items.content: Vitamins A, C, B‑complex and zinc contribute to immune defense.

items.title: Brain development
items.content: Omega‑3 fatty acids and DHA support neural development and cognitive function.

items.title: Digestive health
items.content: Prebiotics and moderate fiber aid normal bowel function.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Children with known cow‑milk allergy may react to the formula.

items.title: Added sugars
items.content: The product contains added sugars; follow the recommended serving size.

items.title: Improper reconstitution
items.content: Too concentrated a solution can strain kidneys, while overly diluted mixes may not meet nutritional needs.

content.title: How to Prepare
content.content: Mix the powder with warm (not hot) water, following the ratio indicated on the package (typically 1 scoop per 30 ml water). Stir thoroughly until smooth, then let it cool to a comfortable temperature before feeding.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, use within 30 days and keep the lid tightly sealed.
